root_cause.text: In the IPv6 FIB ECMP handling, fib6_add_rt2node() cleared RTF_ADDRCONF on an existing gateway route, making it newly qualify for ECMP without ever being inserted into the fib6_siblings list, which broke fib6_nsiblings accounting.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that after commit f72514b3c569, clearing RTF_ADDRCONF on a route “that has a gateway” makes rt6_qualify_for_ecmp() return true even though “this route was never added to the fib6_siblings list,” causing a sibling count mismatch and BUG_ON in fib6_add_rt2node(); the patch fixes this by adding `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family` to avoid clearing the flag on gateway routes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent clearing IPv6 addrconf/prefix route flags on existing routes that have a gateway next hop.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the clearing of RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT on iter->fib6_flags was extended by adding an additional conjunctive check: !iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family. Previously the flags were cleared whenever rt->fib6_flags lacked both RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT; now they are cleared only if that is true and the iter next hop has no gateway family set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT from being removed from an existing route entry when that entry uses a gateway next hop. As a result, routes associated with a gateway retain those flags instead of being incorrectly downgraded during route insertion/merge processing.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown diff is sufficient because it directly modifies the relevant logic inside fib6_add_rt2node(), the function named in the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present here: when an existing route entry `iter` is updated from a new route `rt`, the new code adds `if (!(rt->fib6_flags & (RTF_ADDRCONF | RTF_PREFIX_RT))) { iter->fib6_flags &= ~RTF_ADDRCONF; iter->fib6_flags &= ~RTF_PREFIX_RT; }`. In particular, `iter->fib6_flags &= ~RTF_ADDRCONF;` explicitly clears `RTF_ADDRCONF` on an already-existing route. Per the root cause, clearing `RTF_ADDRCONF` on an existing gateway route can make it newly qualify for ECMP without inserting it into `fib6_siblings`, breaking `fib6_nsiblings` accounting. Since this commit introduces exactly that flag-clearing in fib6_add_rt2node() and the snippet shows no accompanying logic to re-evaluate sibling insertion or update ECMP sibling accounting, the vulnerable construct is present. Therefore this function has the bug and does not contain the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The provided function body is sufficient to evaluate the specific root cause because it contains the duplicate-nexthop handling and ECMP sibling accounting logic. The root cause described is that this function used to clear `RTF_ADDRCONF` on an existing gateway route, causing an already-present route to newly qualify for ECMP without being inserted into `fib6_siblings`, breaking `fib6_nsiblings` accounting. In this snippet, there is no statement clearing `RTF_ADDRCONF` or otherwise modifying `iter->fib6_flags` in the duplicate route path. The duplicate-nexthop case at lines 983-996 only updates expiry state and, conditionally, the PMTU metric: `if (rt->fib6_pmtu) fib6_metric_set(iter, RTAX_MTU, rt->fib6_pmtu); return -EEXIST;`. Since the vulnerable construct (clearing `RTF_ADDRCONF` on the existing route) is completely absent from this function body, `has_bug` is false. However, the code also does not show the specific fix associated with the root cause; instead, this commit changes PMTU handling (`Only update MTU metric if it set`). The ECMP sibling logic remains as before, and there is no visible added safeguard addressing accidental transition into ECMP eligibility due to flag clearing. Therefore `is_fixed` is false.
